name: Corrected human cohort: complete lineage and cited field audit
body:
# Corrected human-source cohort v1 — qualification remains open

Released Hitlist 1.78.0 exported 4,071,463 distinct observations from the complete
corrected corpus v4: 4,045,567 MHC-MS and 25,896 binding observations. Human MHC,
reported human peptide source, lengths 8–25; class I 2,711,461, class II 1,353,735,
non-classical 6,267. Both evidence families retain original endpoints, units,
censoring, citation/source IDs, cell types/conditions, MHC typing sets versus assay
restrictions and reviewed lineage. No mapping alternatives are expanded into
extra observations; no flank or unique source-protein context is claimed.

Native manifest SHA-256:
b180eba804532f633a6d61bb350584dbe24f8df4b4b96f02c6ec492c60144372
Parent complete-corpus manifest:
2318bc53cdae228285218991d58fbcc2bd7266327cec1dd3ed9a03b1c944a5b7

## What changed from human-cohort-baseline-v1

The streaming 161-field comparison verifies every original observation ID and
peptide/source/assay/provenance key in identical order. All 7,646,178 contributor
links remain; contributors.parquet and lineage.json are byte-identical to the
original public baseline. There are zero unresolved contributor links. These
links are provenance, not independent biological samples.

89,567 observations change in 11 metadata fields (662,897 changed cells).
61,917 observations gain a condition ID; distinct nonempty condition IDs increase
from 437 to 463. 78,744 rows in this filtered human export explicitly mark predicted
restriction evidence. Sample labels, sample MHC, attribution/resolution and related
condition metadata are corrected. Measurements, units, censoring, peptide sequences
and all other exported fields are unchanged. The original baseline stays immutable.

Start with comparison-summary.json and comparison-study-counts.tsv.
comparison-value-changes.tsv aggregates each original/corrected value transition
with PMID, reference title/IRI and an explicit observation count. The small
comparison-preview.tsv shows the first three changed cells per PMID/field; it is
not representative. comparison-changed-cells.tsv.gz contains every changed cell
with observation ID and source keys. Values are JSON-encoded to preserve missing
versus empty versus literal strings. The comparison recipe and its hash are frozen
separately from the earlier raw-index comparison.

## Inspect and reuse

The five native files are manifest.json, training.parquet, identities.parquet,
contributors.parquet and lineage.json. Use the native manifest hash to pin consumer
admission. coverage.json, source_contexts.tsv and field_counts.tsv describe the
whole export; inspection.tsv is the original deterministic first 250 rows per
kind/class (1,378 total), not a representative sample. This broad preview happens
to remain unchanged; use the dedicated change reports to inspect the corrections.

1,081 nonempty PMIDs, 21 supplementary files, 133 cell-line names, 28 cell types
and 495,220 source contexts are retained. Source citations and original versus
assigned MHC roles remain separate. Missing/ambiguous values remain explicit.

The export succeeded in 1,473.96 seconds; peak runner RSS 12,472,029,184 bytes,
excluding child processes. CPU 8, RAM 64 GiB, scratch 512 GiB, no GPU, pinned Linux
requirements and released producer. Recipe source is 8fc7f86 (full revision in
publication.json); source files matched that revision, with a completed snapshot
receipt uncommitted at launch. No production/source code was changed during the
run. export-receipt.json records complete runtime, dependencies, input and output
hashes. reproduce.tar.gz preserves exact scripts, lock, parent receipt, comparison
code and original export log. Rerun the pinned human_cohort_modal.py launcher only
against its pinned parent generation; earlier baseline recovery remains separate.

## Qualification limits

Donor, specimen and acquisition identity is unknown for every observation.
Experimental origin is resolved for 57,188 observations across 17 identities;
4,014,275 remain unknown. 2,028,774 rows lack condition IDs, 1,281,272 lack cell
type, and 489,384 supplement rows lack assay method/response/qualitative fields.
Missing units on MS/qualitative evidence are not silently converted into numeric
labels. Original raw export dates remain unverified; optional DepMap is absent.

No train/validation/test membership or fitted-model claim is transferred from the
old baseline. New consumer selection, membership, support and leakage audits are
required with the actual cap/allocation policies. Positive elution is not direct
detectability supervision. Hitlist #678/#680 and Presto #48/#53 remain open.

name: Human-source cohort baseline: native lineage and coverage
body:
# Human-source cohort baseline v1 — not training qualified

4,071,463 distinct observations: 4,045,567 MS and 25,896 binding; human MHC and
reported human peptide source, peptide lengths 8–25. Class I 2,711,461;
class II 1,353,735; non-classical 6,267. Export producer: released Hitlist 1.76.0.
Parent corpus manifest: 7f7f4035d8ec080b26385710d447633dba36ac5cce49008e48e14cf8894f20d5.
Native training manifest: 039efc7854098951b5c10b3fb5b38294452eeb425e367ed1fafdeebddf34b38d.

The native five-file training bundle preserves original observation IDs,
7,646,178 contributor links, original assay endpoints/units/censoring, source
citations, cellular MHC sets versus assay restrictions, conditions and reviewed
lineage. All observations have contributors; no contributor link is unresolved.
These links are provenance, not independent samples. Tables are not expanded
by alternative protein mappings; no flank context is claimed.

Human inspection: coverage.json, source_contexts.tsv, field_counts.tsv, and
inspection.tsv. Missingness is explicit. The preview is the first 250 rows per
evidence-kind/class, 1,378 rows total; it is not a representative sample.
There are 1,081 nonempty PMIDs and 21 supplementary source files.

Qualification limits: donor/specimen/acquisition identity is unknown for every
observation. Only 57,188 observations have resolved reviewed experimental origin,
covering 17 identities; 4,014,275 are unknown. 2,090,691 observations lack a
condition ID and 1,281,272 lack cell type. Units are inapplicable to many MS or
qualitative labels; missing units are not silently imputed. No split, fitting or
independent-experiment performance claim is made. Filtered source dates remain
unverified. The parent corpus retains excluded source organisms and assay families.

This baseline predates corrections #694/#696: single-line source attribution,
DMSO-control metadata, and equivalent reversed-order class-II pair matching.
It must not be presented as containing those fixes. Preserve it for comparison;
a corrected corpus/export requires a new generation. #678/#680 remain open.

Recovery: the original cloud export completed its immutable generation but failed
saving the receipt (#695). All ten original files were recovered through datacache,
hash/size-verified and verified with the native bundle API. Original runtime/RSS
were lost; they remain unknown. recovery-receipt.json records this explicitly.
The original artifact bytes, including native manifests, are unchanged.

name: Corrected complete corpus v4: source lineage and field audit
body:
# Corrected complete corpus v4 — qualification remains open

Released Hitlist 1.78.0 rebuilt this complete generation from exactly the original
pinned IEDB/CEDAR exports and 26 paper assets. The original ci-corpus-v3 and human
baseline remain unchanged. All six stages succeeded in an isolated Linux
requirements lock: environment, sources, indexes, reference, mappings and snapshot.

4,486,991 MHC-MS observations, 814,268 binding rows, 26,537 other-assay rows;
1,506,664 distinct peptides considered for mapping. These are observation counts,
not independent experiments. Original contributors, citations, cell/MHC context,
assay endpoints, units and censoring are retained. Complete mappings use human
Ensembl 112 only; unavailable other-species references remain explicit. The prior
reference cache alone was hash-verified and reused with matching cache-library
versions; observations and mappings were independently rebuilt.

The full 71-field observation comparison verifies identical peptide/source/assay/
provenance keys and order. Exactly 79,406 cells changed, all restriction_evidence
for PMID 32350084: unknown -> predicted. Measurements, peptide sequences and all
other stored observation fields are unchanged. Binding, other assays, contributors,
bulk proteomics, expression and peptide mappings are byte-identical to v3. Current
curation also applies source-arm/class-II-pair fixes at export time; their actual
human-cohort effects are reported in a separate corrected export, not inferred
from this raw-index comparison.

Start with comparison-summary.json, comparison-field-counts.tsv and
comparison-study-counts.tsv. comparison-changed-cells.tsv retains every changed
value with source/assay/provenance key, PMID and reference title/IRI. Values use
JSON encoding to distinguish missingness from literal strings. Row indexes are
zero-based within these exact artifacts, not biological identities.

observations_meta.json is the native complete-generation hash manifest.
publication.json and SHA256SUMS cover the download inventory. build-receipts.tar.gz
contains every stage receipt/log plus exact build recipes, lock, source/reference
pins and comparison code. Frozen build recipe source:
fb64a0c199d91d07f8f7e1fd0da1189b91488a08
(tag experiment-corrected-corpus-20261016). Run each stage in order with
modal run scripts/qualification_modal.py --stage STAGE. CPU 8, RAM 64 GiB,
scratch 512 GiB, no GPU; 85-minute work limit per stage. Runtime and runner-only
RSS (excluding workers) are preserved in the receipts.

This is a complete reproducible software corpus, not a qualified training split.
Raw export dates are unverified; optional DepMap matrices are absent. Unknown
experimental origins, donors, specimens and acquisitions remain unknown. No
partition or independent-experiment performance claim is made. Positive elution
alone is not detectability supervision. #678/#680 remain open; the separate
search-scoped PXD013455 qualification retains its own source and label contract.

name: Reviewed bulk fractionation metadata and complete row audit v1
body: Source-backed fractionation review of the complete original-analysis Bekker-Jensen summaries. Preserves all 2,047,003 peptide-arm and 156,211 protein-arm rows, quantities/order and prior annotations. Includes both full corrected tables, 14-scope citable evidence, before/after counts, original source pins, producer and independent verification code, and SHA-256 hashes. Reported buffer pH, experiment-name pH and unresolved protocols remain distinct. These metadata corrections do not establish the original searched reference, independent biological replicates or new detectability labels.

name: Source-backed bulk experiment counts
body:
# Source-backed bulk experiment counts

Codex / GPT-6, 2026-10-16. Clean executed recipe
`832c95a10d98ab3e37535c7a4362014e4a6518df`, Hitlist 1.81.0 candidate.
[Download all evidence](https://github.com/pirl-unc/hitlist/releases/tag/bulk-experiment-counts-v1).

## Result

The complete 2,047,003-row original-analysis bulk peptide summary preserves every
row, row order, cell line, peptide/protein identity and non-count quantity. Existing
1.80.0 reviewed pH/reference annotations remain unchanged, with their original
values retained. These are peptide-arm rows, not distinct peptides or donors.

The HeLa 46-fraction pool contains three documented MaxQuant experiments:
`HeLa-46fracs-IT-E1`, `HeLa-46fracs-IT-E2`, and `Tryp-46fracs` (138 acquisition runs).
The old observed maximum produced a denominator of two. All 217,514 rows now show
the inventory total of three, but their per-peptide count and reproducibility
fraction are null because legacy aliases collapsed experiment identities. Their
original detected counts remain inspectable. The other 13 scopes retain their
validated counts. No observation is removed when the threshold is omitted.

| Minimum fraction | Legacy filter rows | Qualified filter rows | Rows excluded by correction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Omitted | 2,047,003 | 2,047,003 | 0 |
| 0 | 2,047,003 | 1,829,489 | 217,514 |
| 0.5 | 2,030,253 | 1,812,739 | 217,514 |
| 1 | 1,643,350 | 1,533,246 | 110,104 |

These counts include every enrichment scope for inspection. The public API's
ordinary default additionally selects `enrichment="none"`; pass `enrichment=None`
to inspect all scopes. A threshold excludes unknown evidence even at zero.
`scope-counts.tsv` gives all 14 scope comparisons.

## Source and units

Primary source: [Bekker-Jensen et al., 2017, PMID 28601559](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/28601559/),
[DOI 10.1016/j.cels.2017.05.009](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cels.2017.05.009),
[PRIDE PXD004452](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pride/archive/projects/PXD004452).
The pinned `summary.txt` member was recovered directly from
[SearchResults.zip](https://ftp.pride.ebi.ac.uk/pride/data/archive/2017/06/PXD004452/SearchResults.zip)
using datacache HTTP range extraction. Its 587,345 bytes match SHA-256
`5eb5c41af2c7929be8a9354bf7c9fcb021ead7f47c07d0774a146b352e1a8860`.
The original archive is 21,699,898,516 bytes; only the selected compressed member
and bounded ZIP metadata were fetched, and the complete decoded member was verified.
Every reviewed experiment label, acquisition count and sorted raw-file ID hash
matches this primary summary. The nominal Tryp-39fracs scope contains 40 acquisition
runs, illustrating why fractions and acquisitions must remain separate.

- `n_experiments_possible` is the curated experiment-list cardinality;
  `n_experiments_detected` is a qualified per-peptide count where recoverable.
- `n_replicates_*` are documented compatibility names for those experiment counts.
- `reported_n_replicates_*` preserve original API/source annotations. The raw CSV
  has no denominator column, so its reported denominator remains empty.
- `n_acquisition_runs` is the deposited run inventory; all
  `n_biological_replicates` remain unknown. No donor or specimen independence follows.
- `replicate_count_status`, exact experiment IDs, source URL, summary hash and raw-file
  inventory hash retain the qualification basis. Invalid or missing counts stay null.
- The full audit table additionally includes explicitly named `legacy_inferred_*`
  diagnostics for comparison; those maxima are never the source of a new label.

The assay is bulk shotgun MS, not MHC ligand elution. An MHC allele set does not
apply. Human cell-line identities and enzyme/fractionation/enrichment context are
retained; this audit does not newly curate culture conditions, donor or specimen
identities. It does not turn protocols into a comparable depth ladder or establish
biological replication. Protein abundance values and original source files remain
unchanged. The previously published PXD013455 search-scoped dataset, partitions,
Presto fits and their failed/limited readiness conclusions are unchanged.

## Artifacts and reproduction

The 18-asset publication contains the complete annotated `peptides.csv.gz`, per-scope
counts and evidence, primary summary and recovery receipt, source registry, curation
YAML, frozen audit/projection/fractionation code, independent verifier and its receipt,
plan, publication code, README, manifest and SHA256SUMS. Large inputs and outputs
remain in shared datacache generations. Repository receipts record actual paths,
hashes and publication/verification results.

| Artifact | Bytes | SHA-256 |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Original peptide CSV | 35,074,080 | 3ec65dd05e8ec58c3293e0fb5720570197a8b152cd14778130bae4224106e3d3 |
| Complete annotated peptide CSV | 44,147,940 | 760000129927a762c4de97f3e4c92f608a2dfe17e3d7201d0345adcee0703d4a |

From the pinned clean checkout, with dependencies installed:

```sh
python scripts/audit_bulk_replicates.py --receipt tasks/bulk-replicate-results/audit-receipt.json
python scripts/verify_bulk_replicates.py tasks/bulk-replicate-results/audit-receipt.json --output tasks/bulk-replicate-results/independent-verification.json
```

Actual execution used Python 3.12.6, pandas 2.3.3 and datacache 1.27.1, through isolated
`PYTHONPATH=/private/tmp/hitlist-replicate-provenance:/private/tmp/hitlist175-wheel-import`.
CPU only, no cloud/GPU/model/optimization. The builder streamed 25,000-row chunks in
two passes, taking 84.413 seconds with process peak RSS 403,210,240 bytes; acquisition
and imports are excluded. The independent standard-library row verifier uses no
count-projection helpers and verifies every original row/value, primary inventory,
qualified fraction, historical comparison and aggregate/per-scope result.

The local complete unit suite passed 3,074 tests; 60 focused cases also pass with
37 corpus-dependent cases explicitly excluded. Full CI/integration and exact-main
PyPI deployment remain release gates. This data-only audit introduces no train/test
membership or new predictive performance estimate.

name: Primary HLA Ligand Atlas donor-linked cohort and independence audit
body:
# Primary HLA Ligand Atlas donor qualification

Prospective source audit by Codex / GPT-6, 2026-10-16. Issue #702, within #680/#678.
The clean executed commit, actual results, runtime and verification receipts will
be recorded after execution. No model, optimization or predictions are planned.

## Frozen contract

Use all release 2020.12 primary sample-hit observations and their donor/peptide
reference tables, pinned in `hitlist/data/hla_ligand_atlas.yaml`. Source:
https://hla-ligand-atlas.org/data; Marcu et al., PMID 33858848,
DOI https://doi.org/10.1136/jitc-2020-002071; PRIDE PXD019643; CC-BY-4.0.

Order the 21 namespaced donor IDs by SHA-256 of `atlas-donor-holdout-v1`, newline,
and donor ID. Assign the first three donors to test, next three to validation,
and remaining fifteen to training. Preserve every native observation, sample-hit
row pointer and donor typing. This rule uses neither measurements nor fitted
predictions. Donor groups and reported sample groups must be disjoint; peptide
overlap is measured and fully exported. No sequence-disjoint claim is planned.

The source defines sample groups as donor/tissue/HLA-class triplets. Physical
specimen, aliquot and acquisition identities are not recovered from those keys.
All tissues from one donor nevertheless stay together. Primary benign tissues
are not homogeneous cell types or proof of absence of nonmalignant disease.
All observations are positive eluted ligands; missing observations are not
negative labels. Donor HLA typing is not peptide-specific measured restriction.
Source quality control used binding predictions, a limitation for benchmarking
those predictors; their prediction scores are not new experimental labels.

The historical IEDB cohort is immutable. This source overlaps its Atlas study and
cannot simply be appended as independent evidence. A new prospective consumer
contract must exclude/group mirrors and audit other source contributors before
training. The published historical IC50 fit and failed quality decision remain.

## Reproduction

From the frozen clean checkout, Python 3.12.6, pandas 2.3.3, datacache 1.27.1:

```sh
python scripts/audit_atlas_lineage_v2.py --receipt tasks/atlas-lineage-results/audit-receipt.json
python scripts/verify_atlas_lineage.py tasks/atlas-lineage-results/audit-receipt.json --output tasks/atlas-lineage-results/independent-verification.json
```

The audit stores all primary/derived files in shared datacache generations and
emits a receipt. The independent standard-library verifier imports no Hitlist
reader or audit helpers and replays every source row, identity, typing, partition,
coverage count and overlap. Publication must expose those tables, policies,
source registry, code, hashes and verification, with public downloads checked.

Acquisition note: the first peptide-table request stalled and was interrupted;
a bounded retry succeeded. Both other primary tables were downloaded successfully.
The acquired peptide gzip also matches the independently existing 2025 cache bytes.
No partial source generation or failed audit is treated as complete evidence.

## Executed result and independent review

Successful clean recipe `fc5748b`, candidate Hitlist 1.82.0, retains all **967,449
observations**, **223,246 unique peptides**, **21 donors**, **29 tissues**, and
**418 reported sample groups**. The independent verifier checks all 17 generated
artifacts and reproduces every source-row join, identity, typing and split.

| Partition | Donors | Observations | Unique peptides | Reported sample groups |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Train | 15 | 712,079 | 189,871 | 298 |
| Validation | 3 | 134,015 | 60,686 | 64 |
| Test | 3 | 121,355 | 50,697 | 56 |

Donors, observations and reported sample groups have **zero cross-partition
overlap**. Peptides overlap: 33,241 train/test, 43,232 train/validation, 18,447
validation/test. All 94,920 pair/peptide entries are downloadable. Thus the
**donor-disjoint policy passes; peptide-disjoint policy fails**. Physical specimen
and acquisition identities remain unknown. This source-only cohort is not a
qualified independent addition to IEDB or other Atlas reanalyses.

The original summary recipe `209c7a4` failed independent donor-typing verification
(#703): 19 donor-summary rows were misassociated by a categorical lookup. The
source observations and partitions were correct. The v2 recipe groups typing
within each donor and rejects inconsistent groups. Every artifact except the
summary, executed recipe and execution receipt is byte-identical across the two
runs. The original recipe, receipt and failed-verifier log are preserved, and no
public release or model used the rejected summary. Regressions cover categorical
ordering and conflicting donor typing.

The successful CPU builder took **64.865 seconds**, with process peak RSS
**1,752,547,328 bytes**; acquisition/imports excluded. Python 3.12.6, pandas 2.3.3,
datacache 1.27.1. No cloud/GPU/model/optimization/predictions. Full row tables and
primary bytes remain in shared datacache; source code holds compact receipts.

Public evidence: https://github.com/pirl-unc/hitlist/releases/tag/atlas-donor-lineage-v1
(publication and public verification remain required at this snapshot).

name: PXD013455 HeLa Trypsin/P 46-fraction scope v1
body:
Reconstructed from the public PRIDE PXD013455 reanalysis and the original/reanalysis paper supplements. This release is the HeLa 46-fraction Trypsin/P search scope only.

- 172,033 source observations: 150,855 direct MS/MS and 21,178 match-between-runs observations.
- 1,656,863 candidate occurrences from observed leading-razor parents; 203,635 observed occurrences and 163,994 distinct observed candidate sequences.
- Exact searched FASTA, search settings, all 46 raw-file/fraction assignments, source receipts, citable references and selected supplement tables are included.
- Candidate coordinates, flanks, digestion boundaries, mass/length limits, positive observation links and source-wide presence were independently audited.

The archive contains readable inventory, label policy, coverage, source registry and validation reports alongside parquet tables. Standalone copies of these inspection artifacts and SHA256SUMS are attached.

Unobserved means not observed within this documented search scope; it does not mean intrinsically undetectable. Matching remains distinct from direct MS/MS. The reported fractionation-buffer pH is 8, not a measured gradient pH. No comparable-depth or biological-replicate labels are inferred. Donor/specimen/biological independence remains unresolved. Partitions are not assigned and training readiness is not established.

Archive SHA-256: `9684ae010280fa84ee952439613391fe8f8bce04cceb8818d296615ef636bc9b` (84,673,182 bytes).
Manifest SHA-256: `441f3c66c6e6bc6a90c7cb8c54d0131676c3cb4e7a04ddbd9346061ad8f9d84b`.

The datacache download API is `hitlist.load_pxd013455_bundle()` in merged PR #689 / Hitlist 1.75.0. [Hitlist 1.75.0 is published on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/hitlist/1.75.0/); its public wheels/source and this data archive have been downloaded and hash-verified. Follow-up consumer qualification: pirl-unc/presto#70. Broader qualification: #678 / #680; original PXD004452 FASTA remains #654.

Sources: [PRIDE PXD013455](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pride/archive/projects/PXD013455), [Jarnuczak et al. 2021](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-021-00890-2), [Bekker-Jensen et al. 2017](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cels.2017.05.009).

name: Complete pinned CI corpus v3
body:
Complete corpus rebuilt from pinned IEDB/CEDAR exports and supplement inputs using published Hitlist 1.76.0 and datacache 1.27.1. Producer main: 1c11cb6af7c5e9b1fcec0929d63e7ab1b156ddb3. Manifest format 2; original artifact contract 10.

All ten files belong to one verified generation: observations, binding, other assays, contributors, bulk proteomics, expression, protein mappings, mapping provenance, README and content manifest. The manifest contains SHA-256 and sizes for every payload. Manifest SHA-256: 7f7f4035d8ec080b26385710d447633dba36ac5cce49008e48e14cf8894f20d5.

Build counts: 4,486,991 positive MHC-MS observation rows; 814,268 binding rows; 26,537 other assay rows. Mapping input: 1,506,664 unique peptides. Contributors preserve source overlap and must not be counted as independent measurements. Cell types, conditions, cellular MHC sets and assay restrictions retain separate roles.

This is a reproducible build and CI corpus, not a qualified training split. Mapping is limited to human Ensembl release 112; other reference gaps remain explicit. Source export dates are unverified, optional DepMap matrices were not registered, and unresolved experimental/donor/specimen lineage remains a limitation. Actual training membership, coverage, leakage and held-out fitting are tracked in #680 and #678. Build receipts and reproducibility code: #692.

name: Versioned UniProt reference assets
body:
Human UniProt reference FASTAs for Hitlist's managed release catalog. Sequence payloads are downloaded on demand and remain outside PyPI wheels.

The 2015_10 and 2026_03 human collections include all Swiss-Prot and TrEMBL canonical entries for taxonomy 9606, plus reviewed isoforms. Each JSON receipt records source URLs, source and FASTA checksums, counts, and the extractor checksum. This is broader than the reference-proteome subset.

The historical 2015_10 asset was extracted from complete official archives with published size/MD5 validation. It contains 170,921 sequences in 82,758,858 bytes. Its separate exact-sequence audit explains all 661,142 distinct peptides in the 14 packaged original Bekker-Jensen scopes, with I/L distinct. Sequence compatibility does not establish that the study used this exact search database; issue #654 remains open. The pinned default remains 2026_03.

Attribution: The UniProt Consortium. Data are distributed under CC BY 4.0 (https://www.uniprot.org/help/license). Hitlist performed human-only selection and deterministic FASTA line formatting. Retain published asset bytes; add new releases under new filenames.

name: CI corpus v2
body: Prebuilt hitlist observations corpus for CI integration tests. Includes original build contract and SHA-256 provenance for all five parquets. IEDB/CEDAR-derived; see scripts/publish_ci_corpus.sh.

name: Externalized data assets v1
body: Large paper-derived data files externalized from the PyPI wheel (issue #303) and fetched on-demand via datacache. Provenance: bekker_jensen_2017_* = Bekker-Jensen et al. 2017 Cell Syst (deep HeLa proteome); ccle_nusinow_2020 = Nusinow et al. 2020 Cell (CCLE proteomics); strazar_2023_hla2 = Stražar et al. 2023 Immunity (HLA-II immunopeptidome); abelin_2019_maptac_class2 = Abelin et al. 2019 Immunity (MAPTAC HLA-II). These mirror the original publications and are version-pinned by the hitlist downloads registry.

name: CI corpus v1
body: Prebuilt hitlist observations corpus for CI integration tests. IEDB/CEDAR-derived; see scripts/publish_ci_corpus.sh.
